content.text:
I've submitted, and my pick is **index 5 (Sb fraction 0.37)**. It had the highest EQE I measured, 0.00154%, but that result is weak: every value I measured was close to zero and probably within noise.

I used all 5 EQE measurements:

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.24 | 0.00106 |
| **5** | **0.37** | **0.00154** |
| 9 | 0.50 | 0.00033 |
| 13 | 0.64 | −0.00039 |
| 20 | 0.88 | −0.00086 |

- **Why the signals are so small:** the illumination is only 2.1 eV per photon. Zinc antimonate oxides are generally expected to absorb only well above that, so near-zero EQE along the whole line is what you'd expect.
- **The trend is weak:** the Zn-rich end (Sb 0.24–0.37) was slightly positive and the Sb-rich end was slightly negative. Given how small the values are, that ranking may not hold up.
- **What I didn't use:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements and didn't run the band-gap or stability models. None of these would have added EQE measurements, which is what the score depends on. I chose where to measure by spreading points evenly along the line.
- **What went unmeasured:** 21 of the 26 compositions, including indices 1–4 next to the best result. If anything on the line does better, it is most likely in that Zn-rich stretch.
